questions.question:
**Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.**

A. The movie, B. which you recommended, C. was both interesting D. and entertain.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The issue in the sentence lies in part **D: "and entertain."**
 
• The word "**entertain**" is incorrectly used in this context.
 
• The correct form should be "**entertaining**" to match the grammatical structure of the sentence.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part D** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The movie, which you recommended, was both interesting and entertaining."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A: "The movie,"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **B: "which you recommended,"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **C: "was both interesting"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: **Abrogate**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3 (Repeal)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

 
• The word **"Abrogate"** means to formally put an end to a law, right, or agreement; to annul or revoke something officially. (अधिनियम रद्द करना)

 

 
• **Example:** The government decided to abrogate the outdated law that no longer served its purpose.

 

 

 
• **"Repeal"** is the correct synonym for "abrogate." It means to officially cancel or revoke a law, regulation, or act. (निरसन करना)

 

 
• **Example:** Parliament voted to repeal the controversial tax law after nationwide protests.

 

 

 
• Hence, we can conclude that the most appropriate synonym of **"Abrogate"** is **"Repeal"**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3 (Repeal)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Institute** (संस्थापित करना): To establish, organize, or introduce something, typically a system, rule, or law.

 

 
• **Example:** The school decided to institute a new dress code policy.

 

 

 
• **Enact** (अधिनियमित करना): To make a bill or proposal into a law or to perform a role in a play.

 

 
• **Example:** The government plans to enact legislation to protect endangered species.

 

 

 
• **Approve** (अनुमोदन करना): To officially agree to or accept something.

 

 
• **Example:** The board approved the proposal to expand the company’s operations overseas.

questions.question: **Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrasal verb:** She was so overwhelmed with tasks that she had to ____ some responsibilities to her assistant.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**hand over**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__

• The phrasal verb "**hand over**" means to pass or transfer control or responsibility to someone else.

• In the context of the sentence, the assistant is being given some responsibilities, making "**hand over**" the most appropriate option.

• **Options 1, 2**, and **4** do not fit the context of transferring responsibilities.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"She was so overwhelmed with tasks that she had to **hand over**__ some responsibilities to her assistant."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

• **Option 1: "hand out"** is incorrect as it refers to distributing items, not transferring responsibilities.

• **Option 2: "hand down"** is incorrect as it implies passing something to someone of the next generation, not delegating tasks.

• **Option 4: "hand in"** is incorrect as it means submitting something, not delegating responsibilities.

questions.question:
Which of the following sentences uses the word "close" with the **same meaning** as in the following sentence?

"Please be sure to close the door when you leave"

options.text: She lives very close to the library.
The museum is close to the park.
It’s a good idea to close all the windows before it starts to rain.
He keeps his family photos close to his bed.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"close"** has multiple meanings based on context. It can mean to shut or secure something (e.g., a door, window, or container), or it can refer to proximity or nearness. (Hindi meaning: बंद करना / पास होना)

 
 
• **Example:** Please close the door when you leave. (यहां "close" का मतलब है "दरवाजा बंद करना।")
 

 
• In the given sentence, the word **"close"** is used to mean "to shut or secure something," specifically the door. (Hindi meaning: बंद करना)

 
 
• **Example:** It’s a good idea to close all the windows before it starts to rain.
 

 
• Hence, the correct answer is **Option 3**, as it uses "close" with the same meaning as the given sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1:** She lives very close to the library. (पास)
 
 
• **Explanation:** Here, "close" refers to physical proximity or nearness, not shutting something.
 
• **Example:** The school is close to the market.
 
 

 
• **Option 2:** The museum is close to the park. (पास)
 
 
• **Explanation:** Similar to Option 1, this usage of "close" indicates nearness or being nearby.
 
• **Example:** The restaurant is close to my house.
 
 

 
• **Option 4:** He keeps his family photos close to his bed. (पास)
 
 
• **Explanation:** In this context, "close" again refers to proximity or nearness in terms of placement, not shutting or securing something.
 
• **Example:** She keeps her diary close to her at all times.

questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: **Sit on the fence**

options.text: To be very decisive about a matter
To refuse to give an opinion or take a side
To be in a neutral, relaxed position

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"sit on the fence"** means to refuse to take a side or give an opinion on a matter. (किसी मुद्दे पर पक्ष लेने या राय देने से इनकार करना)
 
 
• **Example:** During the debate, she chose to sit on the fence and did not clearly support either side.
 
 
• The correct meaning refers to staying neutral or undecided in a discussion, avoiding committing to one side or the other. (तटस्थ या अनिर्णीत रहना)
 
 
• **Example:** Politicians often sit on the fence to avoid upsetting any voter group.
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 1: To be very decisive about a matter** (किसी मामले में बहुत निर्णायक होना) - This means to quickly and firmly make a decision.
 
 
• **Example:** She was very decisive about quitting her job and starting her own business.
 
 

 
• **Option 3: To carefully choose a position** (सावधानीपूर्वक स्थिति चुनना) - This implies selecting a stance or opinion with a lot of thought and consideration.
 
 
• **Example:** He carefully chose his position during the negotiation to ensure the best deal.
 
 

 
• **Option 4: To be in a neutral, relaxed position** (तटस्थ, आरामदायक स्थिति में होना) - This refers to being in a calm or neutral physical state, not necessarily related to decision-making.
 
 
• **Example:** After a long day, she sat in a relaxed position on the couch.

questions.solution:

• **Example:** His attempts to fix the broken clock were futile because it was beyond repair.
 
 
 
• **"Effective"** refers to something that is successful in producing a desired or intended result. (प्रभावी)
 
 
• **Example:** The new marketing strategy was highly effective in increasing sales.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'Futile'** is **'Effective'**.

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

• **Example:** The old phone is useless because it no longer works.
 
 
 
• **Pointless** (निरर्थक): Having little or no sense, use, or purpose.
 
 
• **Example:** Continuing the debate seemed pointless since no one was willing to compromise.
 
 
 
• **Vain** (व्यर्थ): Producing no result or effect; futile.
 
 
• **Example:** Despite her efforts, all her attempts to win the contest were in vain.

**Change the following sentence into the Active form.**

The report is expected to be delivered by the committee next week.

options.text: The committee is expecting to deliver the report next week.
The committee is expected to deliver the report next week.
The committee expects to deliver the report next week.
The committee will deliver the report next week.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Active voice involves a subject performing the action, while in passive voice, the subject receives the action.
 
• The original sentence is in passive voice: "The report is expected to be delivered by the committee next week."
 
• To convert it into active voice, the subject "The committee" is placed at the beginning of the sentence.
 
• The verb "is expected to be delivered" is transformed into the active form "expects to deliver."
 
• The time phrase "next week" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The committee expects to deliver the report next week."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The committee is expecting to deliver the report next week." – The sentence uses the present continuous tense, which is incorrect as it changes the meaning.
 
• **Option 2: **"The committee is expected to deliver the report next week." – This sentence is still in passive voice, not active.
 
• **Option 4: **"The committee will deliver the report next week." – This sentence changes the tense to future simple, which alters the original meaning.

questions.question: **Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.** The tour guide said, "We have been walking for hours, but the ruins we have been looking for are just around this corner, and we will be there in a few minutes."

options.text: The tour guide said that they had been walking for hours, but the ruins they had been looking for were just around that corner, and they would be there in a few minutes.
The tour guide said that we have been walking for hours, but the ruins we have been looking for are just around this corner, and we will be there in a few minutes.
The tour guide said that they had been walking for hours, but the ruins they had been looking for are just around that corner, and they will be there in a few minutes.
The tour guide said that they were walking for hours, but the ruins they were looking for were just around that corner, and they would be there in a few minutes.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The tour guide said that they had been walking for hours, but the ruins they had been looking for were just around that corner, and they would be there in a few minutes.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"We have been walking" becomes "they had been walking"**
 
 
• Pronoun "we" changes to "they" in indirect speech.
 
• Present perfect continuous tense "have been walking" is converted to past perfect continuous tense "had been walking."
 
 
 
• **"are just around this corner" becomes "were just around that corner"**
 
 
• Present tense "are" is converted to past tense "were" in indirect speech.
 
• The demonstrative "this" becomes "that" in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **"we will be there" becomes "they would be there"**
 
 
• Pronoun "we" changes to "they" in indirect speech.
 
• Future tense "will" changes to conditional "would" in indirect speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is converted to indirect speech, so no quotation marks are used.
 
• Reporting clause "The tour guide said" introduces the indirect speech correctly.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *The tour guide said that they had been walking for hours, but the ruins they had been looking for were just around that corner, and they would be there in a few minutes.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "The tour guide said that we have been walking for hours, but the ruins we have been looking for are just around this corner, and we will be there in a few minutes."

 
 
• Fails to convert the pronouns "we" to "they" and does not change tenses correctly.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "The tour guide said that they had been walking for hours, but the ruins they had been looking for are just around that corner, and they will be there in a few minutes."
 
 
• Incorrect tense usage: "are" and "will" are not converted to "were" and "would" respectively.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "The tour guide said that they were walking for hours, but the ruins they were looking for were just around that corner, and they would be there in a few minutes."
 
 
• Incorrect tense conversion: "were walking" implies past continuous, but the original sentence uses present perfect continuous.

questions.question:
**Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:**

P: The restoration project was hailed as a triumph of community and expert cooperation

Q: The valuable texts and historic architecture of the old library were preserved throughout its restoration.

R: The library quickly gained international recognition as a cultural icon.

S: To guarantee the restoration’s correctness, local historians and preservationists collaborated.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph begins with Sentence Q, which introduces the restoration of the library.
 
• **Sentence Q** is the first sentence as it describes the preservation of valuable texts and historic architecture during the library's restoration:
 
 
• "The valuable texts and historic architecture of the old library were preserved throughout its restoration."
 
 
 
• **Sentence S** follows, as it elaborates on the collaborative efforts of local historians and preservationists:
 
 
• "To guarantee the restoration’s correctness, local historians and preservationists collaborated."
 
 
 
• **Sentence P** comes next, as it highlights the success of the restoration project:
 
 
• "The restoration project was hailed as a triumph of community and expert cooperation."
 
 
 
• **Sentence R** is the last sentence, as it discusses the library's international recognition after restoration:
 
 
• "The library quickly gained international recognition as a cultural icon."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **Q, S, P, R**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"The valuable texts and historic architecture of the old library were preserved throughout its restoration. To guarantee the restoration’s correctness, local historians and preservationists collaborated. The restoration project was hailed as a triumph of community and expert cooperation. The library quickly gained international recognition as a cultural icon."
